items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: a couple of tunes that he made famous with Eddie Lang

ctx.x: You’ve had quite an on and off association with Stephane Grappelli.

Yeah. That was something I never planned on, it was the same as going with Benny Goodman. You say to yourself wow, here I am with Benny. I played with Benny a long time and then to add to that, I was called to go with Stephane at the Boston Pops, just a duet, honoring Joe Venuti, who I had played with until he died. And we did a couple of Joe’s tunes, “I’ll Never be the Same” and a couple of tunes that he made famous with Eddie Lang. Then our association began because when Stephane came to the United States he…
Speaking of Joe Venuti, were you ever on the receiving end of any of his practical jokes?

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

ctx.x: You’ve played almost with everybody. I’m wondering if there’s anybody that you felt you missed.

Well I missed Bing Crosby. I never played for Bing. I wish I had but that’s a great history there. Eddie Lang played for him. But I followed him every step of the way. I heard all the records that he made and I always enjoy them. And the next best thing was Frank. And I made some records with him. I played at the White House with Frank and Perry Como. And we put a program together for Reagan, you do this and you do that and we had fun putting it together. Same with Benny. Benny had no music with the sextet. We…
Is there something generally in your career that you are most proud of?
